domain: Robot skill parameter policies with a planner
budget_role: Repeated one-practice-step selection during free time; not the complete remaining-budget optimization used by DP
interaction_model: Composes skill competences through task plans; the selection counterfactual changes one skill competence
diagnostic_cost: Estimates from collected transitions; planning to reach practice states is part of embodied interaction
boundary: III-C shares weights between object instances of a parent skill. It is inaccurate to call the whole implementation independent skill models; the extrapolation and counterfactual are the relevant restriction.

domain: Structured robot skills, TAMP, CMA-ES interaction policies
budget_role: Explicit whole practice-budget allocation to maximize expected downstream planning value
interaction_model: Task-plan dependencies are modeled; competence prediction is parameterized by each skill's own allocation
diagnostic_cost: Domain-specific improvement prior plus online estimates; no adaptive paid diagnostic selection in the reviewed allocation formulation
boundary: Optimization guarantees are conditional on the specified competence and abstract transition model. Uncertain priors are an explicit limitation; do not describe it as universally optimal learning.

status: CoLLAs 2023, PMLR 232:846-860; supersedes the narrower 2022 workshop version for this comparison
domain: RL meta-curriculum; MiniGrid and Habitat navigation
budget_role: Lifetime terminal objective is explicit; algorithm approximates it using local k-iteration target improvement
diagnostic_cost: Meta-training uses before/after validation over many lifetimes; online validation steps are omitted at deployment
boundary: Final paper actually uses task-return histories as context; broader 2022 abstract suggestions about trajectories should not be reported as its implementation. Offline teacher cost is explicitly not the main optimization priority.

domain: LM continual pretraining, fine-tuning, out-of-domain data selection
budget_role: Fixed sample and round budget, final average evaluation-skill loss objective
interaction_model: Directed skill graph with a multiplicative loss-dynamics approximation; graph fixed while sampling adapts
diagnostic_cost: Pairwise graph learning or cheaper short single-skill runs; smaller proxy models can supply the graph
boundary: Short probe runs and pretrained starting points already occur here; neither alone is a novel distinction.

budget_role: Predicts mixture outcomes at target model size and training steps using nested scaling laws
interaction_model: Per-domain loss depends on all mixture components; includes a continual-pretraining retention application
diagnostic_cost: Fits laws using multiple smaller/shorter training runs; does not remove the cost of obtaining these runs
boundary: Do not assert that all prior mixture laws ignore forgetting or finite training duration.

budget_role: Final total loss objective; greedy round-level allocation derived from mixing dynamics
interaction_model: Time-varying matrix estimates all group-loss responses to a mixture
diagnostic_cost: Uses fraction delta of each training round for interleaved diagnostic learning; evaluations add inference overhead
boundary: Zero extra training runs does not mean free validation. The paper explicitly acknowledges evaluation cost. Merely adding short diagnostic training to allocation is insufficient novelty.

domain: Shared LLM policy, multi-domain GRPO/RLVR post-training
budget_role: Online bandit feedback; no explicit remaining-horizon terminal success predictor in the reviewed algorithm
interaction_model: Projected-gradient directional alignment plus local learnability
diagnostic_cost: Reuses training gradients without extra probe rollouts; authors report less than 1% wall-clock overhead in their setup
boundary: Its overhead claim belongs to its GRPO implementation, not SAC. A SAC analogue is an adaptation, not a reproduction of the published algorithm.

status: arXiv preprint v1; very recent at the review cutoff
domain: Robot harness, code/skill hypotheses and memory around frozen foundation policies
budget_role: Physical-episode budget and explicit experiment cost in selection
interaction_model: Code-skill joint effects and hypothesis support, not a shared SAC learning-response model
diagnostic_cost: Expected hypothesis-entropy reduction divided by time/steps/GPU/reset cost
boundary: Information gain is not identical to expected final practice-allocation gain; this is a difference in acquisition target, not a claim that decision-theoretic VOI is new.

domain: PPO and MiniGrid; task scheduling and forgetting
budget_role: Compares curricula and learning/retention trajectories, not a budget-end value predictor
interaction_model: Empirically identifies asymmetric transfer and retention between related tasks
diagnostic_cost: Experimental characterization; no claimed cheap predictive allocation system
boundary: Finding one related-task transfer pair in MetaWorld would reproduce a known type of phenomenon, not establish a general selection rule.

domain: Budget-limited algorithm selection from partial learning curves
budget_role: Training and evaluation share a limited resource budget; anytime area-under-curve objective
interaction_model: Underlying candidate curves are precomputed/revealed, not modified by training a different candidate
diagnostic_cost: Acquiring more curve information consumes budget; meta-data cost is separate
boundary: Its anytime objective differs from our proposed terminal macro success. Shared-policy counterfactual paths cannot generally be reconstructed by concatenating its independent curves.

status: ICML 2024; method cross-checked in arXiv v2
domain: LM domain sampling learned with a proxy model
budget_role: Greedy one-step approximation to target-domain generalization
interaction_model: Gradient alignment with aggregate target gradients
diagnostic_cost: One proxy training stage plus gradient estimates; learned average weights transfer to a base model
boundary: Proxy training and a one-step gradient surrogate differ from finite-horizon online robot success prediction.

budget_role: Inference parameter/latency constraints; not remaining practice budget
interaction_model: Measures one task update's effect on other task losses in a shared representation
diagnostic_cost: Task affinity collected in one training run
boundary: Chooses task groupings/networks; using its affinity for practice allocation changes the decision problem.

status: 2017 preprint; this review uses the original publication/abstract rather than assigning a later journal date
interaction_model: Progress and worsening performance motivate scheduling
boundary: Not used to make detailed claims about implementation cost or finite-horizon optimality.

budget_role: Task selection by adaptive, bandit and actor-critic meta-learners
boundary: No detailed cost or horizon claims are made from the abstract.

domain: Hyperparameter optimization with partial learning curves
budget_role: Pause/resume/start candidate training using partially observed curves
boundary: Adjacent conceptual prior; not treated as a direct robot-task scheduler.

budget_role: Incremental resource allocation across training configurations
interaction_model: Bayesian learning-curve extrapolation with a pretrained surrogate
diagnostic_cost: Single-forward-pass prediction reduces online surrogate fitting overhead
boundary: Cheap predictor inference is distinct from cheap collection of decision-relevant evidence.

budget_role: Does not allocate collection budget in the abstracted formulation
boundary: Optimizer intervention, not a like-for-like sampling baseline under the frozen SAC protocol.

budget_role: Bandit task selection using progress signals
interaction_model: Not used here to assess detailed cross-task dynamics
boundary: Background only; the main novelty comparison rests on closer full-method papers.
